cards.text: Years back, Babylon's army burned the house of God in Jerusalem, and Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, carried God's people off into exile (2 Chronicles 36:19-20). Now Persia's in power, and it's the first year of Cyrus, king of Persia. And friend, the LORD is about to get to work on the most powerful man on the map.

cards.question: The LORD stirs the spirit of Cyrus, king of Persia. Why?

answers.text: To fulfill His word spoken through Jeremiah
To answer the prayers of Cyrus himself
To repay Judah for what Babylon took

cards.text: So Cyrus sends a proclamation all through his kingdom, and he puts it in WRITING. Friend, once a king puts it in writing, that's not a text you can unsend.

cards.question: Cyrus says the LORD, the God of heaven, has appointed him to build a ___ for Him at Jerusalem in Judah.
Cyrus says his own armies won him all the kingdoms of the earth.

cards.text: I bet every exile in Babylon has been waiting a long, LONG time to hear this next line.

cards.question: Cyrus's proclamation says anyone who belongs to the LORD's people may do what?

answers.text: Go to Jerusalem and build the house of the LORD
Send gold to Jerusalem for the house of the LORD
Build a house for the LORD right there in Babylon

cards.text: Packing up your whole life and moving back home costs a LOT. Cyrus covers that in his proclamation too.

cards.question: Cyrus says the men of each region should help the survivors with silver, gold, goods and livestock.
Along with that help, Cyrus mentions a ___ offering for the house of God in Jerusalem.

cards.text: So who packs up? The family heads of Judah and Benjamin, plus the priests and Levites.

cards.question: Everyone who gets ready to go up and rebuild has this in common: God had stirred their spirit.

cards.text: And their neighbors come THROUGH: silver and gold, goods and livestock, valuables, on top of all the freewill offerings. That's a going-away party where nobody bothered with a card. They just brought GOLD.
Then Cyrus brings out something Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from Jerusalem.

cards.question: What does Cyrus bring out that Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from Jerusalem?

answers.text: The articles from the house of the LORD
The crown of Judah's last king

cards.question: Nebuchadnezzar had put the articles from the house of the LORD in the ___ of his ___.

cards.text: Stuck for years in somebody else's place, then pulled out to go back to work? Friend, after my years in that junk drawer, I'm getting emotional over DISHES.

cards.question: Cyrus has Mithredath the treasurer count the articles out to someone. Who?

answers.text: Daniel the chief of the wise men

cards.text: Then the inventory: gold and silver dishes, bowls, utensils and more, 5,400 gold and silver articles in all. Sheshbazzar brings every one of them along when the exiles go up from Babylon to Jerusalem.
Now we meet the people who came up out of captivity in Babylon, headed back to Jerusalem and Judah.

cards.question: They return to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own ___.

cards.text: Coming up with them are eleven men named up front, starting with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak (Ezra 3:2). Remember those two, friend. You'll be seeing them again.

Then comes the count, family by family and town by town: the men of Israel, then the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon's servants. The priests come in by the THOUSANDS. The Levites? Seventy-four.

cards.question: A group comes up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addan and Immer. What can't they prove?

answers.text: That their families came from Israel
That Cyrus had given them permission
That they had paid the king's tax

cards.text: Some families from among the priests search for their family records and can't find them. Friend, I lived years in a junk drawer stuffed with receipts nobody needed, and NOT ONCE was one of them the paper somebody was actually looking for.

cards.question: With no family records, these priests' families are excluded from the priesthood.
The governor orders these priests' families not to eat the most holy things. Until when?

answers.text: Until a priest can consult the Urim and Thummim
Until the house of God is fully rebuilt
Until they have served one full year

cards.text: Add it all up and the whole assembly is 42,360, plus 7,337 servants and 200 singers. Then the animals: horses, mules, camels and 6,720 DONKEYS. Friend, that's not a caravan. That's a traffic jam.

cards.question: When they arrive at the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, some family heads give freewill offerings. What for?

answers.text: To rebuild it on its original site
To build it on a new hill nearby
To buy back its lost articles

cards.question: The family heads give to the treasury for the work according to their ___.

cards.text: It comes to 61,000 darics of gold, 5,000 minas of silver and 100 priestly garments. That's not just money, friend. That's the UNIFORM.

cards.question: In the end, everybody settles together inside Jerusalem.

cards.text: Everybody's home, friend. But there's still a house of God to rebuild, and this story is just getting warmed up.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 9 mentions jam, a food that isn't a cookie and isn't in the passage.

rule.text: In jokes and comparisons, cookies are the only food he mentions.

findings.problem: Jeremiah first appears in this card's right answer, but no card says who he is. The opening card introduces Nebuchadnezzar and Cyrus, but the baker never learns that Jeremiah was a prophet.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing from Ezra 1:3. It is only a teaser, yet it cites 1:3. Its hint that exiles were waiting for this line also points toward going home and away from the 'build right there in Babylon' wrong answer on card 7.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Send gold to Jerusalem for the house of the LORD' is close to true elsewhere in the passage. The proclamation includes a freewill offering for the house of God in Jerusalem (Ezra 1:4), and the family heads give gold to the treasury for the work (Ezra 2:68-69). A baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: 'Packing up your whole life and moving back home costs a LOT. Cyrus covers that in his proclamation too.' This gives away the answer to card 9, which asks whether Cyrus says the survivors should be helped with silver, gold, goods and livestock. 'Cyrus covers that' also suggests Cyrus pays, but the text says the men of each region assist.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card is only a junk-drawer reaction to Ezra 1:7, which cards 14 to 16 already covered. It tells no new moment of the passage and doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Zerubbabel and Jeshua are introduced only as 'son of Shealtiel' and 'son of Jozadak', which doesn't say who they are. The card also has 3 sentences.
